154: 1. **Native owners keep authority.** Source Worlds own egress/departure facts, destination Worlds own ingress/materialization facts, and Host owns Task/uncertainty continuity.

102: ## Network continuity boundary
103: 
104: Workstation owns physical route selection and exposes it as explicit transport capabilities rather than asking each Agent or domain to understand interfaces, VPNs, or policy-table numbers. The current `ambient` profile follows the machine's ordinary route and deliberately makes no global-reachability guarantee. `native-a` and `native-b` are HTTPS CONNECT sidecars bound to loopback; each sidecar runs under a dedicated policy-routing identity, opens only public IPv4 TCP/443 destinations, never terminates TLS, and therefore lets the caller retain its own filesystem and credential authority while the outbound socket follows a VPN-independent native path. `netprofile show <profile>` returns a deterministic `profileDigest` covering the transport profile and referenced route profile. Effectful execution is fail-closed: `netprofile run --expect <profileDigest> <profile> -- <absolute executable> ...` refuses stale bindings, projects the selected HTTPS transport through standard proxy environment variables, and exports both profile name and digest to the child. Applications that do not honor HTTPS proxy variables are not covered by this profile.
105: 
106: Cloudflare control-plane ingress consumes the same native route substrate. `ordivon-cloudflare-production-a.service`, `ordivon-cloudflare-production-b.service`, and `ordivon-cloudflare-canary.service` run under the two native routing identities, while a local DoH stub at `127.0.0.55` keeps edge discovery independent of VPN DNS. The two native profiles are **transport/connector redundancy**, not a claim that two physical WANs always exist. When two native defaults are present, A and B select different physical paths even if WSL mirrors them onto the same IPv4 prefix and gateway. When only one native path exists, both profiles deliberately converge on it and the doctor reports reduced physical-path diversity as a warning. Destination reachability remains a measured capability: one native path can reach Cloudflare and DeepSeek while still failing GitHub. `netprofile matrix` labels its output `truthRole=point-in-time-observation` and timestamps both the matrix window and each target probe; an old matrix is evidence of what was observed, never durable current network truth. World consumes a selected transport and does not become a network router; Runtime remains the owner of local execution and need not add network routing to `ExecutionProfile`.
107: 
108: `netcontinuity` closes a failure mode that route structure cannot detect. A VPN may leave its adapter, services and capture routes present while its real data plane is dead; in that state tables 201/202 can remain structurally correct while Windows WFP still blocks both native egress identities. The continuity observer therefore combines Surfshark capture state with bounded destination probes through `ambient`, `native-a` and `native-b`, and writes a point-in-time observation under `/root/.local/state/ordivon-workstation/network-continuity`. The observer never mutates VPN state. `failover-direct --expect <observationDigest>` is a separate effect: it only accepts a fresh `vpn_capture_half_dead` observation, re-observes the fault, requires an Administrator Windows token, releases Surfshark's capture, reconciles the native route tables and proves at least one direct destination capability. `restore-vpn --expect <failoverReceiptDigest>` starts Surfshark and invokes its own UI `connect_button`, then requires both capture routes and ambient destination service before claiming restoration. These explicit effects are intentionally not an automatic timer policy; a future Windows-native Runtime privilege plane should own durable elevated execution rather than relying on ambient WSL interop elevation.
109: 
110: `surfpath` adds a separate Workstation-owned egress capability without promoting Surfshark into network authority. Secret authority remains outside the repository: manual WireGuard configs live under the Surfshark secret root, while imported OpenVPN TCP/UDP configs plus the two-line `auth-user-pass` authority live under the OpenVPN secret root. `surfpath catalog` projects only safe transport metadata and config digests. WireGuard execution is pinned to an exact upstream `wireguard-go` revision and receipted binary digest; OpenVPN execution is bound to the exact Workstation package version and `/usr/bin/openvpn` digest. The provider catalog therefore distinguishes `wireguard`, `openvpn-tcp` and `openvpn-udp` as separate transport variants rather than treating one Surfshark location as one path.
111: 
112: `surfpath discover --write` probes bounded tuples of native ingress, protocol, logical Surfshark node and currently resolved endpoint IP inside transient network namespaces. WireGuard qualification requires a real handshake; OpenVPN qualification requires `Initialization Sequence Completed`. The Linux OpenVPN runtime overlay pins the observed endpoint IP, references the external credential authority, explicitly declares `dev-type tun`, admits the provider's legacy CBC fallback during cipher negotiation, and ignores Surfshark's Windows-only `block-outside-dns` push without modifying the source `.ovpn` authority. In every protocol, a successful tunnel is still insufficient: actual Cloudflare egress plus required destination service are separately observed. Qualified paths are ranked, but ranking is advisory; the observation records `recommendedPathDigest` and `rankedPaths` rather than silently granting execution authority to rank 1.
113: 
114: Effectful use is scoped and Agent-selected. `surfpath run --expect <observationDigest> --path <pathDigest> -- <absolute executable> ...` accepts only a fresh schema-v2 observation and only a path digest that was qualified in that exact observation. It revalidates the current ingress, transport config digest, exact provider binary identity and exact Surfshark endpoint binding, reconstructs the selected WireGuard/OpenVPN tunnel, and re-probes required destinations before running the child. Frozen destination addresses from discovery are tried first, while current path-local Surfshark DNS answers may be used as fallback because CDN addresses are reality rather than durable authority. The child receives protocol, ingress, node, endpoint, path digest and observation digest through `ORDIVON_SURFSHARK_*` variables; application-level destination selection remains application-owned. The Windows Surfshark session and machine default route are not modified. Transient namespaces/rules and the temporary `ip_forward` lease are removed on normal completion. Pre-tunnel Surfshark endpoint hostname resolution is still environment-dependent; an independent global endpoint-discovery resolver remains future continuity work rather than a hidden P1 claim.
115: 
116: The retired `cloudflared-production.service` and `cloudflared-canary.service` units are hash-guarded legacy authority because their default routing followed Surfshark. `agent:apply` removes only the exact retired unit versions recorded in `workstation.toml`.
117: 
118: ## Bounded acceptance and WSL lifecycle recovery
119: 
120: W10 separates routine invariant acceptance from explicit deep inspection. `task doctor` is the bounded Agent gate: it should return a machine-readable answer quickly even when part of the workstation is degraded. `task doctor:deep` retains slow or externally coupled checks such as resource/status reporting, live network dumps, DNS repetition, restic integrity, mirror parity, and secret scanning. Deep checks are valuable evidence, but they must not make the basic authority gate unbounded.
121: 
122: The bounded doctor therefore verifies static provider authority without executing a provider merely to ask for metadata. npm version authority comes from the pacman-owned `/usr/lib/node_modules/npm/package.json`; pnpm version authority comes from the repository `packageManager` field plus the pure-Python resolver and exact installed version path. This matters because a provider startup can exercise unrelated substrate APIs.
123: 
124: W10 found that the live WSL network namespace could enter a partial rtnetlink failure: multiple processes were stuck in uninterruptible `D` state at `rtnl_dumpit`, including `ip` dumps and Node/npm processes. Killing the parent or applying a userspace timeout cannot reliably terminate such a task. The doctor now detects existing rtnetlink dump stalls by reading `/proc` without opening netlink, reports one root substrate error, marks dependent route observations as skipped warnings, and sets `restartPending=true`. While that condition exists, Agents must not repeatedly create new link/route dump probes. A WSL lifecycle refresh is the recovery boundary; after restart the route/link surface must be re-proved before the node is accepted as healthy.
